# 1964 Freedom Summer Trail

> > A self-guided audio tour and historical trail documenting Hattiesburg, Mississippi's pivotal role in the 1964 Freedom Summer civil rights movement.

This site preserves the history of Hattiesburg's civil rights activism, featuring stories of Vernon Dahmer, Mt. Zion Baptist Church, Freedom Schools, and voter registration efforts. Created by VisitHATTIESBURG and featuring oral histories from participants like Cameron Rackley and Larry Blackman.

## Key Topics

- Freedom Summer 1964
- Hattiesburg, Mississippi
- Vernon Dahmer
- Mt. Zion Baptist Church
- Civil Rights Movement
- Voter Registration

- Forrest County Courthouse

- Mississippi Heritage

- VisitHATTIESBURG

## Overview & Introduction

- [1964 Freedom Summer Trail - Follow the historic path of the civil rights movement in Hattiesburg, MS.](https://hburgfreedomtrail.org/): Homepage for Hattiesburg's 1964 Freedom Summer Trail & audio tour
- [FREEDOM SUMMER - 1964 Freedom Summer Trail](https://hburgfreedomtrail.org/about-freedom-summer/): Overview of 1964 Freedom Summer in Hattiesburg, Mississippi's largest site

## Trail Stops & Historic Sites

- [Vernon Dahmer Memorial - 1964 Freedom Summer Trail](https://hburgfreedomtrail.org/vernon-dahmer-memorial/): Stop 10: Memorial to martyred civil rights leader Vernon Dahmer
- [Mt. Zion Baptist Church - 1964 Freedom Summer Trail](https://hburgfreedomtrail.org/mt-zion-baptist-church/): Stop 12: The 'Civil Rights Church' central to Freedom Summer activities
- [Hattiesburg Community Center - 1964 Freedom Summer Trail](https://hburgfreedomtrail.org/hattiesburg-community-center/): Stop 3: Former Freedom School & civil rights planning site on Dewey St.
